title: The integer-scaling criterion for C-realizability
source: Alberto Borobia and Roberto Canogar, “A simplification of the C-realizability criterion for the Nonnegative Inverse Eigenvalue Problem for integers”, arXiv:2401.07857 (2024), Conjecture 31. https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.07857
statement: Let $\{\frac{\lambda_1}{\alpha_1},\ldots,\frac{\lambda_n}{\alpha_n}\}$ be a multiset of rational numbers, and let $p=\operatorname{lcm}(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)$. Here $C_{\mathbb{Q},3}$-realizability and $C_{\mathbb{Z},3}$-realizability refer to the corresponding realizability criteria for the Nonnegative Inverse Eigenvalue Problem. **Integer-scaling criterion.** If $\{\frac{\lambda_1}{\alpha_1},\ldots,\frac{\lambda_n}{\alpha_n}\}$ is $C_{\mathbb{Q},3}$-realizable, then it is $C_{\mathbb{Q},3}$-realizable if and only if $\{p\cdot\frac{\lambda_1}{\alpha_1},\ldots,p\cdot\frac{\lambda_n}{\alpha_n}\}$ is $C_{\mathbb{Z},3}$-realizable.
summary: A rational multiset is C_{Q,3}-realizable exactly when its p-scaled integer multiset (p the least common multiple of the denominators) is C_{Z,3}-realizable; in fact every rational C3 derivation can be replaced by an integer one at scale p, and conversely. The C3 rules are those of the source's Theorem 7 and Definition 9: start from {0}, join two realizable multisets, raise the Perron root, or transfer a positive amount from the Perron root's partner to a nonpositive entry. The proof normalizes a derivation so that a leader absorbs finished blocks one at a time while an outstanding debt is passed up, and then shows that every step can be chosen as an integer in a closed-form region (the leaders are fixed by their terminal values and losing leaders are frozen), which is the integer-rounding statement no prior paper gives. Lean defines C3 inductively over an ordered ring, proves the unconditional direction rational-to-integer and its converse, and checks that C3 over ℤ holds for {1, −1} and fails for {−1}.
paste_summary: Proved. Borobia and Canogar's Conjecture 31 (arXiv:2401.07857): a rational multiset {λ_i/α_i} is C_{ℚ,3}-realizable if and only if its scaling by p = lcm(α_i) is C_{ℤ,3}-realizable, for the C-realizability criterion of the nonnegative inverse eigenvalue problem.
caveat: Possible shorter routes: Marijuan and Moro (2021, 2024) describe real C-realizability by linear inequalities with ±1 coefficients after a real 'downward shift'; turning that into the integer statement still needs an integer-rounding lemma no paper states, which this proof supplies. Whether the Soto S_p → C construction of Borobia, Moro and Soto (2008, Theorem 3.7) is integer-preserving is unchecked (publisher-only; a PDF for the user); if it is, the result is a few lines from published theorems (cross-model reviewer: not routine 0.60, about 0.35 in that case; final checker 0.6-0.65). The Lean follows a reorganized proof written by the Claude Opus 5.5 Lean lane (same ideas as the reviewed GPT-6.1 Sol proof); PAPER.md sections 4-7 are the proof of record. The final check was by a separate Opus lane (same model family as the packager) because GPT-6.1 Sol hit its usage limit; a Sol re-check after 2026-11-26 is advisable.
